statement: The Knuth–Morris–Pratt (KMP) string search first preprocesses the pattern into its LPS array (longest proper prefix that is also a suffix).

You are given a string pattern of length m. For each index i, lps[i] is the length of the longest proper prefix of pattern[0 … i] that is also a suffix of pattern[0 … i]. A proper prefix is shorter than the whole string, so lps[0] = 0.

Build the array in O(m) time: keep the length len of the current matched prefix, extend it when pattern[i] equals pattern[len], and on a mismatch fall back to len = lps[len − 1] rather than starting over. Return the array lps.

examples.explanation: For the prefix "ababab" (i = 5), "abab" is both a prefix and a suffix, so lps[5] = 4. At i = 6 the "c" matches no prefix, so the value drops to 0, and the final "a" matches the first character, giving lps[7] = 1.
All letters are different, so no prefix ever reappears as a suffix and every entry is 0.
